title: Bad Leaders, False Comfort, True King
overview: God condemns the kings and prophets who have misled Judah with comforting lies, and promises a just king from David's line and a gathering of the scattered people.

parts.label: Failed shepherds, gathered sheep (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: The shepherds are Judah's kings and rulers, who were meant to care for the people but let them be scattered into exile. There is a play on words: they did not look after the flock, so God will look into what they have done, and he promises to bring the scattered people home under better leaders.

parts.label: A righteous Branch for David (vv. 5-8)
parts.note: A new shoot will grow from David's royal family tree, which looked cut down, and this king will rule justly. His name, rendered 'The LORD our righteousness' or 'The LORD our righteous savior,' may echo and outshine the name of Judah's last king, Zedekiah, which means 'the LORD is righteous,' and Christians have long read this king as pointing to Jesus.

parts.label: A homecoming greater than Egypt (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: People used to swear oaths by the God who freed Israel from Egypt. This promised return from exile will be so great that it replaces that story as the one they swear by.

parts.label: Corrupt prophets and priests (vv. 9-15)
parts.note: Jeremiah is shaken to the core because religious leaders, even in the temple, are living immorally and encouraging wrongdoing instead of stopping it. Once the northern kingdom's prophets spoke for the god Baal, and now Jerusalem's own prophets are compared to Sodom and Gomorrah, two cities remembered for wickedness and destruction.

parts.label: Peace that is not true (vv. 16-22)
parts.note: These prophets keep promising safety to people who ignore God, but they never stood in his 'council,' pictured like a king's inner circle where advisors hear his plans. A real message would have called people to change their ways, and instead a storm of judgment is coming.

parts.label: Dreams, false messages, and the 'burden' (vv. 23-40)
parts.note: God sees everything, including prophets who pass off their own dreams and recycle each other's lines as his message, which is as worthless as straw next to grain beside his word that burns like fire and breaks like a hammer. The Hebrew word for a prophet's 'message' also means 'burden,' and people were apparently using it glibly, so God bans the phrase and answers only with a promise to cast them off; scholars are unsure of the exact sense, but it ends with a stark threat of exile and lasting shame.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the promised return and righteous king were fulfilled in Judah's return from Babylon, in Jesus and the church, or still await a future restoration of Israel in its land.
think: When have you found yourself trusting a voice mainly because it told you what you hoped to hear?
